question.text: In GP-LP nomenclature used in foreign LLP-form AIFs, who are 'Limited Partners' and who is the 'General Partner'?

answer.text: GP = investors; LPs = manager and sponsor.
GP = custodian; LPs = auditors of the fund.
GP = the manager/sponsor (day-to-day control); LPs = contributing investors (passive, capital only, limited liability except in cases of fraud).

explanation.text: The Logic: In foreign LLP-form AIFs, the General Partner (GP) is the manager or sponsor that runs day-to-day operations of the fund. The Limited Partners (LPs) are the passive investors who contribute capital and do not participate in management. Per the workbook (page 103), in most foreign jurisdictions the manager is the General Partner and investors are Limited Partners. Page 101 supports investors as passive, non-managing capital contributors in the LLP form, with limited liability except in cases of fraud. The Trap: Inverting GP/LP roles, or mapping the roles to SEBI/custodian/auditor, is nonsensical but tempting for candidates unfamiliar with the convention. Note that the LLP form generally limits the liability of all partners except in cases of fraud, so blanket 'unlimited liability' for the GP is not accurate in the LLP context. Note: Distinguish foreign LLP-form AIFs from US-style limited partnerships, where the general partner traditionally has unlimited liability. The workbook's discussion is grounded in the LLP form, where liability is limited.
